topics.title: Personalized Agent-based Image Enhancement
topics.usage: Hello, everyone.

topics.title: Project background
topics.usage: Personalized image retouching should reflect individual preferences.

topics.title: Existing methods and our core idea
topics.usage: AdaInt and RSFNet can require user- or expert-specific training.

topics.title: Project goals and achievements
topics.usage: Our three goals are automatic retouching without instructions, adaptation to unseen users without fine-tuning, and multiple editing candidates.

topics.title: User stories and functional requirements
topics.usage: FR-01 uses the current image and history for automatic enhancement.

topics.title: Acceptance criteria and constraints
topics.usage: Acceptance checks map to all three requirements: predict without instructions or the query target; adapt using eight historical pairs and no weight update; and generate multiple candidates.

topics.title: Modelling user preferences
topics.usage: Early image-similarity retrieval achieved approximately 30% accuracy.

topics.title: Overall system architecture
topics.usage: Stage 1 learns a low-dimensional retouching representation from original and expert-edited images.

topics.title: Stage 1 · Retouching encoder and decoder
topics.usage: The encoder receives the original, target and pixel-wise difference: nine channels in total.

topics.title: Understanding the retouching space
topics.usage: The retouching space is continuous and directional.

topics.title: Stage 2 · Transformer-based conditioning
topics.usage: Eight historical pairs provide image features and edit vectors.

topics.title: Conditional Flow and candidate generation
topics.usage: The conditional flow learns an invertible mapping between retouching vectors and a Gaussian base.

topics.title: Testing strategy and quality assurance
topics.usage: We test reconstruction, prediction quality, unseen-user generalization, conditioning ablations, candidate coverage and computational cost.

topics.title: Datasets and evaluation protocol
topics.usage: FiveK contains 5,000 originals and edits from five experts.

topics.title: Test cases and requirement coverage
topics.usage: The nine checks are grouped by requirement.

topics.title: Retouching space reconstruction evaluation
topics.usage: Reconstruction reached 28.5 dB on FiveK and 28.2 dB on PPSD.

topics.title: Quantitative results on FiveK
topics.usage: FiveK mean Top-1 PSNR was 23.562 dB.

topics.title: Comparison with existing methods
topics.usage: Our reported FiveK and PPSD results provide context against existing methods.

topics.title: Ablation studies
topics.usage: The complete model achieved 23.5 dB.

topics.title: Multimodal evaluation and test limitations
topics.usage: Multiple sampled candidates improve Best-of-K target coverage.

topics.title: Discipline knowledge, implementation and tools
topics.usage: The system combines convolutional image encoding, learned LUTs, Transformer conditioning and Conditional Normalizing Flow, implemented with Python, PyTorch and CUDA.

topics.title: Client feedback and architecture evolution
topics.usage: We explored semantic controls, dynamic grouping, memory, and similarity retrieval before adopting conditional density modelling.

topics.title: Project management and collaboration
topics.usage: Our team used GitHub for version control and collaboration, and Zoom and WeChat for communication.

topics.title: Individual contributions
topics.usage: The nine members contributed across research, implementation, evaluation, presentation and coordination.

topics.title: Reflections, limitations and conclusion
topics.usage: Our contribution is modelling a distribution of edits rather than one fixed output.
